# Task-directed member-contrast transport

## Decision

**No distinct new learning operation survives this assessment.** A valid construction exists: propagate the complete member mean and `k` globally aligned mixtures of member contrasts, reconstruct private messages, and fit the mixtures using the deployed pooled prediction. This is a mean-preserving, task-trained low-rank communication bottleneck. Fisher-weighted low-rank compression, output-distortion rank allocation, ensemble factor distillation, task-trained GNN communication, and learned edge coordinate transport already have inspected primary precedents. None of those papers is claimed to contain this exact assembly; the assembly does not by itself establish substantive novelty.

Two explicit obstructions are useful. **First, a rank below the full contrast dimension cannot universally preserve pooled predictions with arbitrary private downstream Jacobians.** **Second, independent node bases do not commute with the unchanged graph operator.** Adding edge transports repairs coordinate alignment only; it cannot recover discarded source components and has vector-bundle/sheaf overlap and extra edge cost.

The remaining research hypothesis is narrower than generic task-trained compression: **do this source's private suffixes induce a stable, globally aligned, low-dimensional member sensitivity span across nodes, layers and inputs?** Such a property could explain why a small number of contrast channels suffices at lower total cost. It is an unverified structural hypothesis, not a new objective, update rule, theorem, or admitted experiment. This packet stops the branch as a new-method claim.

No `k×k` edge map can recover arbitrary discarded source components. Learned free transports can improve a newly trained model but change the residual graph operator; they do not restore exact multiplication by the original `P` without assumptions. Decoding to the full ambient member axis before aggregation restores a well-defined projected-source operator, but requires full-width sparse transport and forfeits the advertised channel saving.

Neural Sheaf Diffusion defines node/edge vector spaces and restriction maps, with off-diagonal blocks `−F_vᵀF_u`, explicitly identifies orthogonal sheaves with connection Laplacians, learns asymmetric edge maps from endpoint features, and studies their costs [N1–N3]. Equation (7) is an ambient-coordinate connection of the same broad form. NSD is not a frozen ensemble compressor, and its normalized sheaf Laplacian is not this source's directed mean `P`; its method is nevertheless direct prior overlap for “local task basis plus learned edge transport.” Calling that repair a new principle would be unsupported.

## 5. Nearest inspected primary methods

Every row below is based on a full primary method body, with versioned URLs, raw hashes and exact passages in `PRIMARY_PASSAGES.json`. These are the inspected versions, not claims about their latest version or publication status. Search metadata is discovery only.

| Primary source and passages | Inspected operation | Consequence for this branch |
|---|---|---|
| [Mind the Approximation: Fisher-Weighted SVD Compression for ViTs](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.07155v1), §3.1–3.2, §4.1–4.3 [F1–F4] | Fisher-whitened truncated SVD under a Kronecker metric; analyzes weight-sharing cross-token and activation-gradient assumptions; FACTS retains token-local coupled statistics. CoRS profiles output KL at candidate layer ranks and allocates ranks under a FLOP constraint, allowing uncompressed layers. | Downstream-weighted rank selection and output-distortion budget allocation are established. Its parameter-space curvature and vision-local prior do not establish a member-axis metric or justify dropping graph/node cross terms here. Its additive rank profile is a proxy, not a guarantee for jointly compressed layers. |
| [Knowledge Distillation of Uncertainty using Deep Latent Factor Model](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.19290v1), §3.1–3.4 [L1–L4] | A student learns a mean and factor-loading function; teacher functions are independent realizations of a Gaussian process. EM fits the latent model at design points; inference generates members from the estimated process. | “Full mean plus a few learned ensemble factors” and uncertainty distribution distillation are established ingredients. It distills functions rather than transporting fixed private graph states, assumes a Gaussian latent process, and does not guarantee identity with a finite source ensemble. Its shared-body/fixed-head comparison also locates ordinary multi-head reconstruction overlap. |
| [Learning Accurate, Efficient, and Interpretable MLPs on Multiplex Graphs via Node-wise Multi-View Ensemble Distillation](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.05864v1), §4.1–4.2 [M1–M3] | Distills graph teachers to a graph-free MLP using CE and KL. MGFNN+ fits node-wise weights over individual views plus the whole teacher; the coefficient matrix uses a global basis and node-feature-dependent low-rank reparameterization, with entropy regularization. | Task-trained low-rank ensemble coefficient selection and preserving more than a merged teacher target are established. View/teacher weights at the output are not signed intermediate contrast coordinates; output-local coefficients face no graph-coordinate commutation claim. |
| [Communication-Efficient Cooperative Localization: A Graph Neural Network Approach](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.08135v1), §III-B–III-E [C1–C4] | VQ-MPNN learns a projection encoder, a codebook shared across nodes and a decoder; nodes exchange indices and reconstruct neighbor states before message computation. The objective combines localization MSE with VQ reconstruction/codebook/commitment terms, including stopgradient. Its bit accounting includes packet overhead. | Direct precedent for training a GNN communication compressor on the downstream task. VQ operates on node-state latent codes rather than member contrasts and uses surrogate gradients for discrete quantization. This candidate's differentiable linear projection needs no such surrogate. Float-channel reduction alone is not a bit-rate or latency result. |
| [Neural Sheaf Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.04579v1), §2, §3, §6 [N1–N3] | Learns local edge restriction maps and propagates vector-valued signals through a sheaf/connection Laplacian; includes diagonal, orthogonal and general maps and their normalization costs. | Strong overlap for repairing local member bases with learned coordinate transports. It supplies no exactness theorem for source compression under the original `P`, and equal ambient spans reduce to a global gauge choice. |
| [Favour: FAst Variance Operator for Uncertainty Rating](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.13036v1), §3–4.1 [V1–V2] | Propagates means/covariances; approximates covariance as diagonal plus low rank. Alternating diagonal projection and subspace iteration minimize a Frobenius covariance reconstruction objective without forming the full propagated matrix. | Low-rank uncertainty transport is established. Frobenius covariance approximation is not pooled prediction distortion, and these covariance factors are not identifiable source member modes. This overlap is assessed only; the parent develops moment closure separately. |
| [An Analytic Solution to Covariance Propagation in Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.16163v1), §3.1–3.4 [W1–W2] | Propagates mean and full covariance; assumes Gaussian input at each nonlinearity and derives a covariance series for element-wise activations, including GELU. | Analytic moments do not provide an assumption-free substitute for deterministic private member trajectories, member–head association or LayerNorm. Merely adjoining a moment channel is not an uncovered direction. |
